name: adaptive-controller
description: Does the AdaptiveController earn its complexity? (docs/research.md Open Question 6, issue #9.) Compares the controller-driven run against the best fixed-weight token_importance run at an EQUAL TOKEN BUDGET (capacity 128/layer, keep_ratio 0.25 at context 512), plus the full_cache reference for quality_delta. The controller run additionally carries a device byte ceiling of 0.125 MiB -- half of the 0.25 MiB its 128 tokens/layer natively occupy -- which is what gives the controller a decision to make: without a binding constraint every decision would be a trivial retain. allow_recompute is False (the runner sets it explicitly): RECOMPUTE is in the action vocabulary but re-running the model is the runtime's job, and a decision that cannot fire must not appear in the trace. On single-tier (CPU) hardware the controller's least-lossy over-budget action, offload, is infeasible, so the trace shows compress; on a CUDA machine the same config exercises offload first. Known caveat, same as --compressor: the quality pass runs its own uncompressed cache, so quality does not price the controller's compression.

runs.notes: reference: no eviction, no compression, no offload
